description:
FILED s473t5d (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 5 CHECK 1.

`lib/IO.pm:147` is

  sub ungetc { Carp::croak('IO::Handle::ungetc is not implemented under PCL') }

and t/io/scalar_ungetc.t calls it on its second row, so 17 of the file's 19
rows never run.

WHAT THE FILE ASKS FOR (perl 5.40.3):
  open my $io, '<', \$s;  getc $io;
  $io->ungetc(ord 'A')  returns the ORD it was given (not 1, not the handle)
  getc($io)             is then chr(65)
  $s                    is UNCHANGED ("foo") -- the pushback is in the handle,
                        not in the scalar
  and then ELEVEN ungetc calls in a row, each returning its own ord, followed
  by eleven getc calls that read them back in reverse.

SO IT IS A PUSHBACK STACK, and that is why CL's `unread-char` is not the answer:
it allows ONE character and only immediately after a read-char.  The shape is a
per-handle pushback vector that `%p-getc`/`p-read`/`p-readline` drain before
touching the stream -- i.e. a handle-level facility, not an IO::Handle method
body, with `lib/IO.pm`'s `ungetc` becoming a thin call into it (rule 9a: the
pushback is core handle state, the method is module surface).

ALSO IN THE FILE, and not this task's: row 1 asserts
`Internals::SvREADONLY($s,1)` makes `$s = 'bar'` die "Modification of a
read-only value" -- that is NS:`Internals::*` C-level introspection, announced
already ("PCL: Internals::SvREADONLY: a SCALAR is not implemented ? ignored").

ROWS: t/io/scalar_ungetc.t 18 blessed fail rows + 17 shortfall.
subject: `IO::Handle::ungetc` is an explicit croak in lib/IO.pm; t/io/scalar_ungetc.t loses 17 rows, and the shape needs a pushback STACK, not CL unread-char
